messages:
Alex: heads-up — nightly paged+flash variant started spitting NaNs in generation on a customer repro. Looks like softmax overflow only when fp8 path + KV incremental decode + high concat batch sizes hits.
Marta: ugh. seeing logs? quick summary pls
Alex: posted short stack in CI artifact. key bit: pre-softmax logits grow unexpectedly on some long sequences (~>1e4) and then fp8 path saturates and softmax returns inf -> NaN downstream.
Sachin: any recent kernel selector changes? we landed adaptive-batch for paged kernels last week.
Alex: yes that change plus "merge small KV segments" optimization. repro appears when merge increases effective token window in a single kernel call.
Priya: can you paste the repro command? i'll try locally
Alex: sure:
```
# repro
python -m infra.attn_repro --model tiny --seq 8192 --steps 50 --use_fp8 --kernel paged_flash --merge-kv=true
```
Marta: quick profiler snapshot from my run: the pre-softmax logits have a long tail; max(logits) ~ 1.2e4 before softmax. With bf16 path max ~ 1.2e2. So accumulation/scale mismatch in fp8 path likely.
Sachin: sounds like missing rescale before softmax when we stitch merged KV blocks. FP8 accumulators need an explicit scaling schedule otherwise you get exponent blowup.
Priya: would adding a small clamp/eps in softmax help as short-term mitigation? e.g. softmax(x - max(x)) then clip max to 1e2
Alex: tried that — clamps prevent NaN but quality drops for edge cases. Also masks/normalization logic expected to keep magnitudes reasonable; this feels like we double-count some attention logits when merge-kv=true.
Marta: can we add a circuit-breaker in kernel selector: if dynamic range (max-min) > threshold -> fall back to bf16 kernel for that batch. Cheaper than full disable.
Sachin: I like that. cheap heuristic: compute a small sketch over logits (min/max) from the first microbatch, if range>THRESH -> route to bf16 kernel. Need microbench to see perf impact.
PerfBot: perf regression alert: fallback-to-bf16 heuristic estimated +18% p90 latency on 4k seq in perf model; but avoids NaNs.
Priya: alternative: adjust accumulation path in fp8 kernel — scale accumulators down when merging KV segments. Might be more correct but riskier and more invasive.
Alex: plan proposal:
- short term: selector circuit-breaker (Marta) + softmax clamp opt-in flag for customers
- mid term: implement accumulator rescale in fp8 paged_flash kernel (Sachin)
- tests: add synthetic property tests that run incremental decode merge combos and assert no NaNs and stable logits distribution
Marta: i'll open a canary PR for selector heuristic. config flag in runtime: `runtime.attn.fp8_circuit_breaker_range = 500` default off.
Sachin: i'll start a branch for accumulator rescale. will add unit that compares fp8 accumulation to bf16 baseline on random inputs and long sequences.
Priya: i'll assemble a minimal failing trace and attach to the ticket. also add perf bench to measure fallback hit rate.
Alex: ticketing: REDWOOD-ENG-4321, add labels: eng-runtime, perf, fp8, paged-flash. Please reference when PRs land.
Marta: quick note — if we do selector at batch-level we need to ensure deterministic routing for tests (seed + stable hashing). else can be flaky.
Sachin: agreed. will add deterministic selection in unit harness. also will log routing decision for observability.
PerfBot: CI: nightly bench for paged_flash scheduled. will run selector-canary on next run and post results.
Alex: thanks all. prioritize selector canary and repro artifact in ticket. follow-ups tomorrow.
Priya: ack, grabbing repro now :thumbsup:
Marta: thanks — adding myself to PR review. :eyes:
